lessons.title: Past Simple: Regular Verbs
warmup: 🕰️ Yesterday
What did you do yesterday? Tell me one thing. / Kecha nima qildingiz? Bir narsa ayting.
🔁 Review routines
Revise L21 verbs: wake up, go to school, do homework. / L21 fe'llarini takrorlang.

x: I watched a film last night.
They visited the museum last week.

grammar.rule: Regular past: verb + **-ed** (play → played, watch → watched)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Yesterday I ___ football. → a) play b) played c) playing
She ___ her homework last night. → a) finish b) finished c) finishes

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: cleaned / We / last / house / the / week / .

reading.title: A Busy Day
reading.passage: Yesterday was a busy day for Tom. He started his day at seven o'clock. He studied English for one hour. Then he helped his father in the garden. In the afternoon he visited his grandmother. She cooked delicious soup. Tom watched a film in the evening and finished his homework. He was tired, but happy.
qs: What time did Tom start his day?
What did Tom do in the garden?
What did his grandmother cook?
How did Tom feel at the end of the day?

listening.title: What Did They Do?
qs: What did Mark do in the morning?
Where did Anna go?
What did the children play?
listening.script: Listen. Yesterday Mark played tennis in the morning. Anna visited the museum with her class. The children played football in the park. In the evening everyone watched a film together.

writing.title: Write About Yesterday
writing.task: Write 4 sentences about your yesterday. Use regular verbs: watched, played, helped, studied, cooked.
writing.uz: Kechagi kuningiz haqida 4 gap yozing. Muntazam fe'llardan foydalaning.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people what they did yesterday. Write their answers. / 3 kishidan kecha nima qilganini so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 verbs in present + past 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about your yesterday · Reading: re-read 'A Busy Day', answer 4 questions · Speaking: tell your family about your day.
teacher: Review present routine verbs first, then add -ed.
Drill the -ed endings (/t/, /d/, /id/) — walked, cleaned, visited.
Watch for 'yesterday I play' — remind that yesterday needs past.
Writing task: model 2 sentences first, then students write.

lessons.title: Past Simple: Irregular Verbs
goals: 🔄 Use common irregular past verbs (went, had, saw)
warmup: 🔄 Quiz
What is the past of 'go'? Of 'eat'? / 'go'ning o'tgan zamonini ayting.
🕰️ Review regular verbs
Quick drill: watch → watched, play → played. / Muntazam fe'llarni takrorlang.

x: We went to the park yesterday.
My friend came to my house.
He took a book from the shelf.

grammar.rule: Irregular pasts: **go→went, have→had, do→did, see→saw, eat→ate, buy→bought**
mistake: Wrong: *I go to the park yesterday.*
Right: *I went to the park yesterday.*

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Yesterday we ___ to the zoo. → a) go b) went c) gone
She ___ a cake for us. → a) make b) maked c) made

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: went / to / I / the / market / yesterday / .
a / film / saw / They / last / night / .

reading.title: A Weekend Visit
reading.passage: Last Saturday, Aziza and her brother went to their uncle's farm. They saw many animals — cows, sheep and a white horse. They ate fresh bread and drank cold milk. Aziza took some photos. Her brother helped the farmer. In the evening they came home tired and happy. Aziza said: 'What a great day!'
qs: Where did Aziza go on Saturday?
What animals did they see?
What did Aziza's brother do?
What did Aziza say at the end?

listening.title: What Happened Yesterday?
qs: What time did Ali get up?
What did Ali eat for breakfast?
Where did Ali go after school?
listening.script: Listen. Yesterday Ali got up at half past six. He had bread and milk for breakfast. After school, he went to his friend's house. They played games and made pizza. Ali came home at seven o'clock.

writing.title: A Story in the Past
writing.task: Write 5 sentences about a visit or trip you made. Use: went, saw, ate, had, came.
writing.uz: Qilgan safaringiz haqida 5 gap yozing. Berilgan fe'llarni ishlating.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What did you have for breakfast?
Where did you go last weekend?
Yes, I saw an action film.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell a story about your last weekend using 5 irregular verbs. / Oxirgi dam olish kuni haqida hikoya ayting.

quiz: Correct: 'I go to the market yesterday.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 irregular verbs (present+past) 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences with irregular pasts · Reading: re-read 'A Weekend Visit' · Speaking: tell your weekend story to your family.
teacher: Play memory games with the irregular pairs (matching cards).
Teach irregulars in groups by sound: go/went, see/saw, eat/ate.
Watch for 'goed'/'buyed' — correct to went/bought.
Encourage storytelling; students love sharing real weekend stories.

lessons.title: Food and Quantities
goals: 🛒 Talk about what there is to eat
warmup: 🍎 Food race
Name 5 foods in 20 seconds. / 20 soniyada 5 ta ovqat ayting.
🛒 In my kitchen
Say: 'In my kitchen there is... / there are...' / Oshxonangizdagi narsalarni ayting.

x: There is some rice in the bag.
There are some apples on the table.
There is some sugar in the tea.
There is some water in the bottle.

grammar.rule: **some** (positive) / **any** (negative & questions) · countable: a/an, -s · uncountable: no plural

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Is there any milk? → a) Yes, there is b) Yes, there are c) Yes, some

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: some / is / There / in / milk / the / fridge / .

reading.title: The Shopping List
reading.passage: Mother made a shopping list. 'We have some rice and sugar, but there isn't any bread. There aren't any eggs, and there isn't any milk.' Aziz took the list and went to the shop. He bought some bread, a packet of eggs and a bottle of milk. He also bought some chocolate for himself — but he didn't tell mother!
qs: What food is in the house?
What did Aziz buy?
What did Aziz buy for himself?

listening.title: In the Kitchen
qs: Is there any milk?
Are there any eggs?
What is on the table?
listening.script: Listen. In the kitchen there is some bread and some cheese. There is some milk in the fridge. There aren't any eggs. On the table there are some apples and a bottle of water.

writing.title: Write About Your Kitchen
writing.task: Write 5 sentences about your kitchen: 3 with 'some' and 2 with 'any'.
writing.uz: Oshxonangiz haqida 5 gap yozing: 3 tasi 'some', 2 tasi 'any' bilan.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: There's some cheese and some water.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Check your fridge at home and say 4 sentences with some/any. / Uydagi muzlatkichni tekshirib, 4 gap ayting.

quiz: Correct: 'Is there any rice?' → 'Yes, there are.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 foods 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences with some/any about food at home · Reading: re-read 'The Shopping List' · Speaking: talk about your fridge with your family.
teacher: Use real or drawn food items to make some/any physical.
Explain countable (can count: eggs, apples) vs uncountable (rice, water).
Watch for 'some' in negative sentences.
Shopping-list activity is a great model for real life.

lessons.title: How Many / How Much
warmup: 🍎 Count it
How many chairs in this room? How many windows? / Bu xonada nechta stul bor?
🥛 Guess
How much water is in this glass? / Stakanda qancha suv bor?

x: How much sugar do we need?
We have a lot of rice.

grammar.rule: **How many** + countable (apples, eggs) · **How much** + uncountable (milk, sugar)
grammar.uz: Sanoqli bilan 'how many', sanoqsiz bilan 'how much'
ex: **How many** eggs are there? — There are six.
**How much** milk is there? — There's a little.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: How ___ sugar is in the tea? (many/much)
How ___ students are in your class? (many/much)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: How much rice is there? → a) There's a lot b) There are five c) It's big

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: much / How / sugar / we / do / need / ?

reading.title: At the Market
reading.passage: Nodir went to the market with his mother. 'How many carrots do we need?' his mother asked. 'Three kilos,' Nodir said. 'And how much rice?' asked the seller. 'Two kilos, please.' Nodir also wanted a little chocolate. His mother smiled: 'How much chocolate do you want?' 'A lot!' said Nodir, and everyone laughed.
qs: How many kilos of carrots do they need?
How much rice do they buy?
What did Nodir want at the end?

listening.title: Write the Quantity
qs: Carrots: ______
listening.script: Listen and write. We need a little milk — one litre. We need six eggs. We need two kilos of carrots. And we need a lot of apples for the party.

writing.title: My Shopping List
writing.task: Write a shopping list with quantities: 'two kilos of rice, a bottle of milk...' (5 items).
writing.uz: Miqdorlari bilan xarid ro'yxati yozing (5 ta narsa).

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: How much tea do you drink?
How many apples do you want?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your partner about their kitchen: 'How many...? How much...?' (3 questions). / Juftingizga 3 ta savol bering.

quiz: Correct: 'How many sugar do we need?'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 quantity words 3× · Grammar: 6 how many/how much questions + answers · Reading: re-read 'At the Market' · Speaking: use how many/how much at home.
teacher: Reinforce countable vs uncountable with physical examples.
Drill the answer patterns: 'There are six / There's a little.'
Watch for 'how much' with countable nouns.
Shopping-list writing is practical and fun.

lessons.title: At the Supermarket
warmup: 🛒 What's in a supermarket?
Name 5 things you can buy. / Supermarketda nima sotiladi?
🧺 Role the basket
Quick review: 'How much is the bread?' / Narx so'rashni takrorlang.

x: I put the apples in the basket.
The milk is in aisle three.
He uses a trolley for big shopping.
There is a discount on bread.

grammar.rule: Polite requests: **I'd like... / Can I have...?** + quantities
ex: **I'd like** a kilo of rice, please.
**Can I have** a bottle of milk?

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I'd ___ a kilo of apples, please. (like/want)
___ I have a packet of biscuits? (Can/Do)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: At the checkout you say: → a) I'd like a bag, please b) I sleep c) Good morning

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: like / I'd / a / of / kilo / rice / , / please / .

reading.title: A Quick Shopping Trip
reading.passage: Malika went to the supermarket with a short list. First she took a trolley. In the fruit aisle she put two kilos of apples. In aisle four she found a packet of biscuits and a bottle of juice. At the checkout, she said: 'I'd like a bag, please.' The cashier smiled: 'That will be fifteen thousand som.' Malika paid and took her receipt. She was home in ten minutes.
qs: Where did Malika put the apples?
What did she buy in aisle four?
What did she ask for at the checkout?
How much did she pay?

listening.title: At the Checkout
qs: What does the customer buy?
How much is it?
What does the customer ask for at the end?
listening.script: Listen. Customer: 'I'd like a kilo of cheese, please.' Cashier: 'Here you are.' Customer: 'How much is that?' Cashier: 'Thirty thousand som.' Customer: 'Can I have a bag, please?' Cashier: 'Of course.'

writing.title: Write a Dialogue
writing.task: Write a 4-line dialogue at the checkout between you and the cashier.
writing.uz: Siz va kassir o'rtasidagi suhbatni yozing (4 qator).

speaking.title: Role-Play: At the Shop
table: Thank you! How much is that?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Go shopping with your family and say 'I'd like...' in English! / Xaridda inglizcha gapirib ko'ring.

quiz: Complete: '___ I have a bottle of juice?' (Can/Do)
What do you ask at the end? → 'How ___ is that?'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 supermarket words 3× · Grammar: write a shopping dialogue · Reading: re-read 'A Quick Shopping Trip' · Speaking: practice your dialogue with your family.
teacher: Set up a classroom shop with real objects and price labels.
Model the dialogue once, then students repeat in pairs.
Watch for 'I want a bread' — drill 'I'd like some bread'.
Use play money for realism.

lessons.title: Jobs and Occupations
goals: 💼 Talk about what people do at work
warmup: 🎭 Job mime
Act out a job — students guess! / Kasbni imo bilan ko'rsating.
💭 My family
What does your father do? Your mother? / Otangiz nima ish qiladi?

x: My father is a bus driver.

grammar.rule: **What does he/she do? — He/She is a...** (+ what they do at work)
ex: **What does** your father **do**? — He's a driver.
Otangiz nima ish qiladi? — U haydovchi.
U nima ish qiladi? — U hamshira.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: What does he do? → a) He is a farmer b) He does a farmer c) Yes, he does

reading.title: People in My Family
reading.passage: Let me tell you about my family. My father, Akmal, is a farmer. He grows wheat and vegetables. My mother, Dilnoza, is a teacher. She teaches English at a big school. My older brother is an engineer — he designs buildings. My aunt is a nurse at the city hospital. And me? I want to be a pilot when I grow up!
qs: What does Akmal grow?
Where does Dilnoza teach?
What does the brother do?
What does the writer want to be?

listening.title: Who Are They?
qs: What does the first man do?
What does the woman do?
Where does the nurse work?
listening.script: Listen. This man is a driver. He drives a bus in the city. This woman is a chef. She works in a big restaurant. This nurse works at the hospital and helps doctors every day.

writing.title: Write About Jobs
writing.task: Write 4 sentences: 2 about people in your family and 2 about your dream job.
writing.uz: Oilangizdagi kishilar va orzu kasbingiz haqida yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What do you want to be?
I want to be a pilot.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people about their jobs. Report: 'He/She is a...'. / 3 kishidan kasbini so'rang.

quiz: What do you want to be?
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 jobs 3× · Grammar: 6 questions + answers about jobs · Reading: re-read 'People in My Family' · Speaking: tell your family about today's lesson.
teacher: Job mime is a great warm-up — students love acting.
Drill 'does' with he/she; watch for 'He do'.
Use family photos if students bring them.
Connect to L77 (careers) — plant the seed.

lessons.title: Supermarket Role-Play Workshop
goals: 💰 Use quantities, prices and some/any together
Miqdor, narx va some/anyni birga ishlatish
warmup: 🛒 Shop words
Name as many supermarket words as you can in 30 seconds. / 30 soniyada supermarket so'zlarini ayting.
🧺 Quick dialogue
Review: 'I'd like... / How much is that?' / Suhbatni takrorlang.

practice.title: Build Your Shop
items: Make 5 items with price labels (in som). / 5 ta narxli mahsulot yasang.
One of you is the customer, one is the cashier. / Biri xaridor, biri kassir bo'lsin.
Use: 'I'd like... / Can I have...? / How much is that?' / Berilgan gaplarni ishlating.
Swap roles and do it again. / Rollarni almashtiring.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: The customer asks for bread: → a) I'd like some bread b) Give me bread c) Bread!

speaking.title: Role-Play Time
speaking.body: Perform your shopping dialogue for the class. Use quantities and prices. / Xarid suhbatingizni sinfga ko'rsating.

speaking.title: Swap Roles
speaking.body: Now you are the cashier. Serve your partner politely. / Endi siz kassirsiz — xushmuomala bo'ling.

lessons.homework: Write your role-play dialogue and practice it at home. / Rolli o'yin suhbatingizni yozing va mashq qiling.
teacher: Workshop: set up a 'shop' with real or drawn items.
Let students rehearse before performing.
Praise polite language ('I'd like', 'Thank you').
Give feedback on pronunciation of prices.

lessons.title: Speaking Circle: Talking About Yesterday
goals: 🕰️ Use regular and irregular past verbs
'Did you...?' savollarini berish va javob berish
warmup: 🕰️ One thing
Tell one thing you did yesterday. / Kechagi ishingizdan birini ayting.
🔄 Past review
go→went, eat→ate, see→saw. Say the past! / O'tgan zamonni ayting.

x: I visited my aunt last week.

practice.title: Yesterday Story Cards
items: What time did you get up? / Soat nechada turdingiz?
What did you have for breakfast? / Nonushtaga nima yedingiz?
Where did you go? / Qayerga bordingiz?
Who did you see? / Kimni ko'rdingiz?
What did you do in the evening? / Oqshomda nima qildingiz?

speaking.title: My Yesterday
speaking.body: Speak for 2 minutes about your yesterday: morning, afternoon, evening. Use past verbs. / Kechagi kuningiz haqida 2 daqiqa gapiring.

speaking.title: Interview
table: Yes, I did. / No, I got up late.
Yes, I went out. / No, I stayed home.

speaking.title: Active Listening
speaking.body: Write 3 things your partner did yesterday. / Juftingizning 3 ta ishini yozing.

lessons.homework: Write your full yesterday story (8-10 sentences) with past verbs. Practice it aloud. / Kechagi kuni haqida hikoya yozing.
teacher: Speaking circle: keep each turn short and supportive.
Have a 'story chair' — one student narrates while others listen.
Correct past-tense errors gently by echoing the right form.
This consolidates L41-42 — no new grammar.

lessons.title: Present Continuous
warmup: 🏃 What am I doing?
Teacher mimes an action — students say: 'You are reading!' / Imo bilan ko'rsataman.
👀 Look around
What are your classmates doing right now? / Sinfdoshlaringiz nima qilmoqda?

grammar.rule: **am/is/are + verb-ing** (do → doing, run → running, write → writing)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: What are you doing? → a) I'm writing b) I write c) I wrote
She ___ now. → a) is sleeping b) sleep c) slept

reading.title: A Busy Park
reading.passage: It is Sunday morning and the park is busy. Look! A man is running with his dog. Two girls are riding bikes. A boy is eating an ice cream. Under a tree, a woman is reading a book. Near the lake, some children are feeding the ducks. Everyone is having a wonderful time on this sunny morning.
qs: What is the man doing?
What are the two girls doing?
Who is reading a book?
What are the children doing near the lake?

listening.title: What Is Happening?
qs: What is the mother doing?
What is the little boy doing?
What are the birds doing?
listening.script: Listen. In this picture, the mother is washing the dishes. The little boy is drawing a picture. His sister is sleeping on the sofa. Outside, the birds are singing in the tree.

writing.title: What Is Happening in Your Classroom?
writing.task: Write 4 sentences about what is happening in your classroom right now.
writing.uz: Sinfda hozir nima bo'layotgani haqida 4 gap yozing.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Watch your family for 1 minute and say what everyone is doing. / Oila a'zolaringizni kuzating va ayting.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about actions now · Reading: re-read 'A Busy Park' · Speaking: describe your home to your family.
teacher: Mime and pictures make the continuous tense concrete.
Drill -ing spelling: run→running, write→writing.
Watch for missing -ing: 'She is cook'.
Compare with L41 past: now vs yesterday.

lessons.title: Making Plans
goals: 📅 Talk about future plans with 'going to'
🗓️ Use time words: tonight, next weekend
🗣️ Ask 'What are you going to do?'
warmup: 📅 The weekend
What are you going to do this weekend? / Dam olish kuni nima qilasiz?
⏰ Review present continuous
Quick drill: 'What is she doing now?' / Hozirgi zamonni takrorlang.

x: We're going to travel next weekend.
I'm going to visit my uncle.
We're going to stay at home.
She's going to buy a dress.
I'm going to meet my friends.
We're going to travel by train.

ex: I **am going to** study English tonight.
She **is going to** visit her aunt.
We **are going to** have a party.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I ___ going to watch a film. (am/is/are)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: What are you going to do? → a) I'm going to sleep b) I sleep c) I slept

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: to / She's / visit / going / aunt / her / .

reading.title: Weekend Plans
reading.passage: Ask the family: what are your plans? 'Tonight we're going to watch a film together,' says Mum. 'On Saturday, Dad and I are going to visit the bazaar,' says Grandmother. 'I'm going to play football with my friends,' says brother. 'And I'm going to finish my book!' says sister. Everyone has a plan — and I am going to help Mum cook dinner!
qs: What is the family going to do tonight?
What are the grandmother and Dad going to do on Saturday?
What is the brother going to do?
What is the writer going to do?

listening.title: What's the Plan?
qs: What is Anna going to do tomorrow?
Where is she going to travel?
Who is she going to meet?
listening.script: Listen. Anna has big plans. Tomorrow she is going to get up early. She is going to travel to Bukhara with her family. There, she is going to meet her cousins and visit the old city.

writing.title: My Weekend Plan
writing.task: Write 5 sentences about your weekend using 'going to'.
writing.uz: Dam olish kuni rejangiz haqida 'going to' bilan 5 gap yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What are you going to do tonight?
Who are you going to meet?
I'm going to meet my cousin.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell your family one plan for tomorrow. / Ertangi rejangizni oilangizga ayting.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 words 3× · Grammar: 6 'going to' sentences · Reading: re-read 'Weekend Plans' · Speaking: discuss your weekend plan with your family.
teacher: Link to L49: now (continuous) vs future (going to).
Use a real calendar to talk about plans.
Watch for missing 'am/is/are'.
Let students plan a real weekend in pairs and present.
